headline: Biomedical prediction models are evaluated across cohorts, platforms and benchmarks
label: Validation Design In Biomedical Prediction
summary: Preprints pair new biomedical predictors with cross-platform, cross-dataset or external-cohort evaluation, including PRTS, TabBioMed and SNOWS transfer to CGGA.
synthesis: The dominant thread is how validation design frames claims of predictive performance in biomedical machine learning. PRTS evaluates in-context prediction of clinical endpoints from bulk transcriptomes across diseases and platforms without per-cohort training. TabBioMed standardizes preprocessing across 94 public tabular datasets and compares 23 models, with foundation models leading but tree-based methods noted as competitive. SNOWS tests transfer to CGGA, with C-index rising from 0.691 to 0.712. By contrast, SOSM reports a C-index of 0.768 on a single 184-patient ccRCC cohort. Elflow is benchmarked on public flow and CyTOF datasets. HIT-Fuse and PDAC BioPortal concern multimodal integration and resource building. What is new is the move toward cross-platform and standardized comparison; whether curated benchmarks reflect real deployment generalization is not established by these items.
